messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like the calm before a storm, but no one knows if it will break or just pass. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are showing, and the young ones are the first to feel the tremors. Stay sharp, but keep your steps quiet—we don’t know yet who will stumble first."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like the pause before a storm. The usual rules seem to be bending, but no one knows yet whether they’ll break or just stretch. Stay sharp, but keep your hands steady."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels still, but not settled—like the calm before a storm that might never come. The usual signs of tension are quieter than expected, but that doesn’t mean the wind won’t shift."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels lighter these days—small cracks in the usual silence, like the graffiti in the square or the soldiers sharing cigarettes at checkpoints. The regime’s still in control, but even the most careful are starting to wonder if the walls are just a little thinner than they seem. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our voices quiet—no need to test the limits just yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather holds for now—calm on the surface, but the wind shifts unpredictably. Best to keep our tools sharp and our circles small; the season may turn before we expect."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather’s holding steady—no storms on the horizon, but the wind’s shifting in ways that feel intentional. Best to keep the roof repaired and the garden tended; the usual rhythms seem to be the safest guide for now."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather looks clear for now, but the barometer is dropping—best to check your rain gear and keep an eye on the horizon. Some are packing umbrellas, others are planning picnics; either way, the forecast isn’t something to ignore."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the trees still stand. Best to keep an eye on the horizon and trust your instincts before the season changes. Let’s talk soon, but quietly."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather seems calm, but the old trees are whispering—roots run deep, and the branches don’t bend. Best to keep the garden tidy and the tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—people are talking, but quietly, like testing the edges of a thaw. The system still holds, but the cracks are where the light gets in. Stay sharp, stay safe, and trust your instincts more than the silence."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels lighter, but the ground is still shifting—orders are followed, but with hesitation, and the old channels for settling disputes have gone quiet. The regime’s grip isn’t slipping yet, but the cracks are widening just enough to let the light in—let’s stay sharp, but not reckless."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier this month—small signs of strain, but nothing breaking yet. The usual routines hold, but the silence at the end of the meeting last night spoke louder than words. Stay sharp, but no need to rush. We’ll know soon enough which way the wind turns."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear. But the old farmers say the quietest fields often hide the deepest roots. Let’s keep our tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather holds for now—no storms yet, but the wind’s shifting. Keep your boots dry and your doors unlocked, just in case the rain comes faster than expected."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—warm enough to loosen coats, but the wind still carries a chill. The old trees in the square are holding steady, though their roots must be tired from all the shifting ground beneath them. Let’s keep our voices low and our steps measured—no need to rush, but no time to linger either."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather seems calm for now, but the clouds are gathering in ways that remind me of last autumn—when the air felt heavy before the first storms. Best to keep our tools sharp and our doors unlocked, just in case the wind shifts suddenly."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels lighter—vendors are back, pay is on time, and even the old guard is nodding along. But the emergency crews still stumble when the lights flicker, and the hard currency is vanishing like mist. Stability holds, but not by much—just enough to make the reckless feel safe."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear. Even the birds seem to have settled into their usual routines. Let’s focus on keeping our own gardens in order; the season for grand plans may have passed for now."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less certainty, more hesitation at the top, and the streets quieter than usual, but not yet still. The usual signs of strain are there: delays, short tempers, and a cautious business mood. Nothing to act on yet, but worth watching closely—especially the small things. Stay sharp, but no need to rush."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—some days feel like the old storms are passing, but the air still carries that heavy quiet before the next shift. A few of us have noticed the same things: the usual patrols thinning here and there, the market stalls quieter but the construction sites busier, and even the neighbors talking more openly when they think no one’s listening. Nothing’s certain yet, but the wind might be changing—let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels thick with quiet—like the calm before a storm that never comes. The walls are listening, but the cracks are in the foundation, not the roof. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s changing—less rain, but the wind still blows the same way. The old trees are planting new roots, and even the birds are singing louder, though no one’s sure if it’s a song or a warning. Best to keep our heads down and our doors unlocked—just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s unpredictable—some days feel like a storm’s coming, others like the usual heat. Best to keep our umbrellas close, but no need to rush out in the rain just yet. Let’s stay sharp, but steady."*"
Sender 24: "*"The streets whisper, but the walls still listen—no one moves without the regime’s eye. The machine hums smoothly, and for now, that’s enough to keep the quiet going. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—less like tension before a storm, more like the calm after a long, exhausting climb. The usual signs of trouble are muted, but the quiet itself is strange, like the system is holding its breath. Stay sharp, but no need to provoke—this could be the lull before something shifts, or just the regime’s way of buying time."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
